hints.title: Keep the previous term constant
hints.body: In the integral, x varies but un−1 is a number already found. Take that number outside the integral, then integrate what remains.
hints.recap: A factor independent of x stays constant during integration.
hints.pitfall: Do not treat the sequence index as a power of x.
hints.pause: Calculate the definite integral and its multiplier.

recall.reminder: A factor independent of x stays constant during integration.

hints.title: Follow the multiplier
hints.body: Use your result to calculate the first few terms from u0=1. Write a formula for un and check it at index zero.
hints.recap: A fixed multiplier between consecutive terms gives a geometric progression.
hints.pitfall: The sequence starts at index zero, not one.
hints.pause: Check the formula obeys the recurrence, then use the requested index.

recall.reminder: A fixed multiplier between consecutive terms gives a geometric progression.

solution:
For fixed n, un−1 is a number independent of x. Thus

un=un−1∫014xdx=un−1[2x2]01=2un−1.

Starting from u0=1, this gives u1=2, u2=4, … and in general un=2n, since each update supplies one factor of 2. Hence u1000=21000.

Answer A.
